stem: A company wants to detect objects, faces and inappropriate content in images uploaded by users.

options.why: Rekognition analyzes images and videos for objects, faces and unsafe content.
Polly converts text to speech, which isn't what this scenario needs.
Transcribe converts speech to text, so it doesn't solve the problem described here.
Comprehend analyzes text, so it doesn't solve the problem described here.

explanation.answer: Amazon Rekognition provides pre-trained image and video analysis, including object detection, face analysis and content moderation.
explanation.concept: No ML expertise is required to use it.

stem: An e-learning company wants to turn written lessons into natural-sounding audio.

options.why: Translate converts text between languages.
Polly converts text into lifelike speech.
Transcribe does the opposite: speech to text.
Lex builds chatbots, so it doesn't meet this requirement.

explanation.answer: Amazon Polly turns text into lifelike speech in many voices and languages.
explanation.concept: Polly and Transcribe are opposites.

stem: A call center wants to convert recorded customer calls into text for analysis.

options.why: Rekognition analyzes images and video, which isn't what this scenario needs.
Polly converts text to speech, which isn't what this scenario needs.
Transcribe converts speech to text, which matches what the question asks for.
Kendra is intelligent search, so it doesn't meet this requirement.

explanation.answer: Amazon Transcribe automatically converts speech to text, with features for call analytics.
explanation.concept: Combine with Comprehend to analyze sentiment in the transcripts.

stem: A company wants to find the sentiment and key phrases in thousands of customer reviews.

options.why: Textract extracts text from documents, so it doesn't meet this requirement.
Polly converts text to speech, so it doesn't solve the problem described here.
Translate converts languages, so it doesn't meet this requirement.
Comprehend uses NLP to find sentiment, entities and key phrases in text.

explanation.answer: Amazon Comprehend is a natural language processing service that finds insights such as sentiment, entities and key phrases in text.
explanation.concept: It doesn't require ML training for common tasks.

stem: An insurance company wants to extract text, tables and form fields from scanned claim documents.

options.why: Textract extracts printed and handwritten text, tables and forms from documents.
Lex builds conversational bots, so it doesn't solve the problem described here.
Rekognition analyzes images but isn't specialized for forms and tables.
Comprehend analyzes text but doesn't read scanned documents.

explanation.answer: Amazon Textract automatically extracts text, handwriting, tables and form data from scanned documents.
explanation.concept: Textract goes beyond simple OCR by understanding document structure.
explanation.examTip: Extract data from scanned forms = Textract.

stem: A bank wants to build a chatbot that understands customer questions by voice and text.

options.why: Translate converts languages, so it doesn't solve the problem described here.
Lex builds conversational interfaces with speech recognition and language understanding.
Polly speaks text but doesn't understand conversations.
Textract extracts text from documents, so it doesn't solve the problem described here.

explanation.answer: Amazon Lex lets you build chatbots and voice bots with automatic speech recognition and natural language understanding.
explanation.concept: Lex integrates with Amazon Connect for contact centers.

stem: A retailer wants to automatically translate product descriptions into ten languages.

options.why: Polly converts text to speech, so it doesn't meet this requirement.
Transcribe converts speech to text, so it doesn't meet this requirement.
Translate provides neural machine translation between languages.
Comprehend analyzes text, so it doesn't meet this requirement.

explanation.answer: Amazon Translate delivers fast, high-quality language translation.
explanation.concept: It supports many languages and custom terminology.

stem: A data science team wants to build, train and deploy its own custom machine learning models on AWS.

options.why: Rekognition offers pre-trained vision models, not custom model building in general.
Comprehend offers pre-trained NLP; it isn't for building custom models in general.
Polly converts text to speech, so it doesn't meet this requirement.
SageMaker AI provides tools to build, train and deploy custom ML models.

explanation.answer: Amazon SageMaker AI is a fully managed service for building, training and deploying machine learning models at scale.
explanation.concept: Use AI services for common tasks; use SageMaker AI for custom models.
explanation.examTip: Build your own ML models = SageMaker AI.

stem: A company wants to build a generative AI application using foundation models from several providers through one API, without managing infrastructure.

options.why: Bedrock provides access to foundation models from leading providers through a single API.
Rekognition analyzes images, which isn't what this scenario needs.
Comprehend analyzes text with NLP, which isn't what this scenario needs.
Lex builds chatbots; it doesn't offer foundation models from several providers.

explanation.answer: Amazon Bedrock is a fully managed service offering foundation models from Amazon and other AI companies through a single API.
explanation.concept: It includes features for customization, knowledge bases and guardrails.
explanation.examTip: Generative AI with foundation models = Bedrock.

stem: A company wants employees to search across internal documents and get precise answers to natural-language questions.

options.why: Lex builds chatbots, so it doesn't meet this requirement.
Kendra is an intelligent enterprise search service.
OpenSearch provides keyword and log search, but Kendra is built for natural-language answers over enterprise content.
Textract extracts text from scanned documents.

explanation.answer: Amazon Kendra uses machine learning to provide intelligent search across enterprise content.
explanation.concept: Kendra connects to many repositories, such as SharePoint and S3.

stem: Developers want an AI assistant that helps write code, explain code and answer questions about AWS inside their IDE.

options.why: Polly converts text to speech, which isn't what this scenario needs.
Transcribe converts speech to text, so it doesn't meet this requirement.
Q Developer is a generative AI assistant for software development and AWS.
Comprehend analyzes text; it isn't a coding assistant.

explanation.answer: Amazon Q Developer assists with coding, debugging and AWS questions in IDEs, the console and the command line.
explanation.concept: Amazon Q Business answers questions over company data.
explanation.examTip: AI coding assistant on AWS = Amazon Q Developer.

stem: A company wants to run SQL queries directly on log files stored in Amazon S3 without loading them into a database.

options.why: Redshift can query S3 with Spectrum but needs a warehouse; Athena is serverless SQL directly on S3.
RDS requires loading data into a database.
DynamoDB isn't for SQL queries over S3 files.
Athena is a serverless query service that runs SQL directly on data in S3.

explanation.answer: Amazon Athena is an interactive, serverless query service that analyzes data in S3 using standard SQL. You pay per query.
explanation.concept: Athena often uses the AWS Glue Data Catalog for table definitions.
explanation.examTip: SQL on files in S3 = Athena.

stem: A data team needs to discover, prepare and transform data from many sources into a data lake, without managing servers.

options.why: Glue is a serverless data integration (ETL) service with a data catalog.
QuickSight visualizes data, so it doesn't meet this requirement.
This streams video, so it doesn't meet this requirement.
Athena queries data but doesn't discover and transform data from many sources into a data lake.

explanation.answer: AWS Glue discovers, prepares, moves and integrates data from multiple sources for analytics, ML and application development.
explanation.concept: The Glue Data Catalog stores table metadata for Athena, EMR and Redshift Spectrum.

stem: A company wants to collect and process clickstream data from its website in real time.

options.why: Glue runs ETL jobs, not real-time clickstream ingestion.
Kinesis collects and processes streaming data in real time.
SQS queues messages but isn't designed for real-time stream analytics.
Redshift analyzes stored data but doesn't ingest real-time streams by itself.

explanation.answer: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams captures and processes large streams of data records in real time.
explanation.concept: Amazon Data Firehose loads streaming data into destinations like S3 and Redshift.

references.title: What is Amazon Kinesis Data Streams?

stem: Business users want interactive dashboards and charts built from company data without writing code.

options.why: EMR runs big data frameworks, which isn't what this scenario needs.
Athena runs SQL queries but doesn't build dashboards.
QuickSight is a business intelligence service for dashboards and visualizations.
Glue prepares data, so it doesn't solve the problem described here.

explanation.answer: Amazon QuickSight provides interactive dashboards, visualizations and natural-language queries for business intelligence.
explanation.concept: It connects to many data sources, including Athena, Redshift and S3.

stem: A company runs large Apache Spark and Hadoop jobs and wants a managed platform for them.

options.why: DataBrew is for visual data preparation.
Athena runs SQL on S3, not Spark and Hadoop jobs.
Batch schedules jobs but isn't a managed Spark and Hadoop platform.
EMR is a managed platform for big data frameworks like Spark and Hadoop.

explanation.answer: Amazon EMR runs big data frameworks such as Apache Spark, Hadoop, Hive and Presto on AWS.
explanation.concept: EMR is available on EC2, EKS and as EMR Serverless.

stem: A company wants to search and analyze application logs in near real time, with full-text search and dashboards.

options.why: OpenSearch Service provides search, log analytics and dashboards.
Athena queries logs in S3 but doesn't provide near-real-time full-text search and dashboards.
Redshift is a SQL data warehouse, not full-text log search.
DynamoDB is a key-value database, so it doesn't meet this requirement.

explanation.answer: Amazon OpenSearch Service makes it easy to run search and log analytics with OpenSearch and OpenSearch Dashboards.
explanation.concept: Common uses include log analytics, application search and observability.
explanation.examTip: Full-text search / log analytics = OpenSearch Service.

stem: A company wants to load streaming data into Amazon S3 automatically, with buffering and format conversion, without writing consumer applications.

options.why: Data Streams needs consumer applications to process and deliver data.
Firehose captures, transforms and loads streaming data into destinations without consumers to manage.
Batch processes batch jobs, so it doesn't solve the problem described here.
SQS is a message queue, not a streaming delivery service.

explanation.answer: Amazon Data Firehose reliably delivers streaming data to destinations such as S3, Redshift and OpenSearch Service.
explanation.concept: It's fully managed and scales automatically.
explanation.examTip: Stream → S3/Redshift with no code = Data Firehose.

stem: An online store wants product recommendations tailored to each customer, without building ML models from scratch.

options.why: Polly converts text to speech, which isn't what this scenario needs.
Comprehend analyzes text, so it doesn't meet this requirement.
Personalize creates real-time personalized recommendations.
Rekognition analyzes images, which isn't what this scenario needs.

explanation.answer: Amazon Personalize uses ML to generate real-time recommendations, such as products, content or rankings.
explanation.concept: It's based on the same technology used at Amazon.com.

stem: A product team is matching AI services to use cases.
prompt: Which TWO pairings are correct? (Select TWO.)

options.why: Translate translates; Lex builds chatbots.
Polly generates speech; Comprehend analyzes text.

options.text: Amazon Textract – extract fields from scanned forms
options.why: Textract reads text, tables and forms, which is exactly what this scenario needs.

options.text: Amazon Polly – detect faces in photos
options.why: Rekognition detects faces; Polly speaks text.
Transcribe converts speech to text, which is exactly what this scenario needs.

explanation.answer: Textract = documents. Transcribe = speech to text. Polly = text to speech. Rekognition = images. Lex = chatbots. Comprehend = text insights. Translate = languages.
explanation.concept: Learn one verb per AI service.
explanation.examTip: Read docs=Textract, hear=Transcribe, speak=Polly, see=Rekognition, chat=Lex.

stem: A company wants to set up a secure data lake quickly and manage fine-grained access to tables and columns centrally.

options.why: Athena queries data lakes but doesn't manage fine-grained table and column permissions.
DataBrew prepares data visually; it doesn't govern data lake access.
EMR processes data but doesn't centrally manage data lake permissions.
Lake Formation helps build data lakes and manage fine-grained access.

explanation.answer: AWS Lake Formation makes it easier to set up, secure and manage data lakes, with column- and row-level permissions.
explanation.concept: It works with the Glue Data Catalog, Athena, Redshift and EMR.
explanation.examTip: Data lake + fine-grained permissions = Lake Formation.

stem: A startup with no ML experts wants to add image moderation to its app quickly.

options.text: Use Amazon Rekognition's pre-trained moderation API
options.why: A pre-trained AI service adds the feature without building models.

options.text: Train a custom model from scratch in SageMaker AI
options.why: This needs ML expertise and time, which isn't what this scenario needs.

options.text: Use Amazon Athena on the images
options.why: Athena queries structured data, not images.

options.text: Write custom image analysis on EC2
options.why: This needs significant effort and expertise.

explanation.answer: AWS AI services like Rekognition provide pre-trained models via APIs, so you can add intelligence without ML expertise.
explanation.concept: Choose SageMaker AI when you need custom models.
explanation.examTip: No ML experts + common task = pre-built AI service.

stem: A team occasionally queries small CSV files in S3 and doesn't want to manage any infrastructure.
prompt: Which service is the MOST cost-effective fit?

options.why: RDS requires loading data and running an instance.
Athena is serverless and charges per query on data in S3.
A cluster costs money even when idle, which isn't what this scenario needs.
EMR Serverless works but is heavier than needed for occasional SQL on small files.

explanation.answer: Amazon Athena is serverless and charges for the data scanned by each query, ideal for occasional queries over S3.
explanation.concept: Use Redshift for frequent, complex warehouse workloads.

stem: A financial company needs to detect potentially fraudulent online transactions using machine learning, without deep ML expertise.

options.why: Textract extracts text from documents, so it doesn't solve the problem described here.
Rekognition custom labels classify images, not transaction patterns.

options.text: Custom models trained in Amazon SageMaker AI
options.why: SageMaker AI provides built-in algorithms and tools that simplify building fraud detection models.
Sentiment analysis doesn't predict fraud from transaction patterns.

explanation.answer: Amazon SageMaker AI offers built-in algorithms, AutoML (SageMaker Autopilot) and managed training for use cases like fraud detection.
explanation.concept: Pre-built AI services cover common tasks; SageMaker AI covers custom predictions.
explanation.examTip: Custom predictions like fraud scoring = SageMaker AI.

stem: A data team is choosing analytics services.
prompt: Which TWO statements are correct? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Amazon EMR is a DNS service
options.why: EMR runs big data frameworks, so it doesn't meet this requirement.

options.text: AWS Glue is a graph database
options.why: Glue is a data integration service, which isn't what this scenario needs.

options.text: Amazon Athena runs SQL directly on S3 data
options.why: Athena queries data in S3 with SQL, so it meets the requirement described here.

options.text: Amazon Kinesis ingests real-time streaming data
options.why: Kinesis handles real-time streams, which matches what the question asks for.

options.text: Amazon QuickSight stores raw data as a database
options.why: QuickSight visualizes data; it isn't a database.

explanation.answer: Athena = SQL on S3. Kinesis = streaming. QuickSight = dashboards. Glue = ETL. EMR = Spark/Hadoop. Redshift = warehouse.
explanation.concept: Analytics services form a pipeline: ingest, store, catalog, process, visualize.
